name: Mint Cream
lede: Mint Cream is a near-white with the faintest green tint, a screen color from the X11 and CSS lists.

sections.title: A list name
sections.body:
Mint Cream is one of the 140 colors in the X11 Color Set, with the hex code #F5FFFA [1]. Paterson files it separately from mint-green, which he describes as the green of the aromatic plant's leaves, a pastel green [1]. It is also a CSS keyword, `mintcream` [2]. The origin of this name is undocumented in our books [1].

The ISCC-NBS system of 1955 would call the swatch a "greenish white" (block 153), 4.2 CIEDE2000 units away, and the nearest name in our learning set is plain white, 5.2 away [3]. Its neighbors in the same list include [[honeydew]], [[lavender-blush]] and [[linen]] [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: In our 23,781-painting archive a color near this one appears in 68 paintings, 0.29% of the total, as photographed [4]. In 75% of the 40 paintings where the within-painting lens finds it, it plays a light, the pale end of the canvas [4]. The earliest dated match is a painting by Filippo Lippi of 1452, and it is most over-represented in paintings from China, 5.3 times the expected rate [4]. The name itself peaks in printed English in the 2010s [5]. Varnish and photography shift whites, so read these as screen colors [4].

origin.named_after: origin undocumented; an entry in the X11 color list
